family.description: This transmembrane domain is found in metal transporter proteins such as cyclin M 1/2 (CNNM). CNNMs are integral membrane proteins that are conserved from bacteria to humans. CNNM family members influence metal ion homeostasis through mechanisms that may not involve direct membrane transport of the ions. Structurally, CNNMs are complex proteins that contain an extracellular N-terminal domain preceding a transmembrane domain, a 'Bateman module', which consists of two cystathionine- beta-synthase (CBS) domains [pfam:PF00571], and a C-terminal cNMP (cyclic nucleotide monophosphate) binding domain [[cite:PUB00088668],[cite:PUB00088669],[cite:PUB00088670],[cite:PUB00088671]]. This entry describes the CNNM transmembrane domain which contains four hydrophobic regions and forms a dimer through hydrophobic contacts between TM2 and TM3, in which each chain is composed of three transmembrane helices (TM1-3), a pair of short helices exposed on the intracellular side, and a juxtamembrane (JM) helix that forms a belt-like structure [[cite:PUB00088669],[cite:PUB00098586]]. The homodimer adopts an inward-facing conformation with a negatively charged cavity containing a conserved pi-helical turn in TM3 that coordinates a Mg2 ion [[cite:PUB00098586]].

causal_graphs.context: POPE/POPG 3:1 vesicles contain 50 uM mag-fura-2 in 20 mM HEPES-KOH pH 7.5, 100 mM KCl, 50 mM NaCl and initially 0.5 mM EDTA. UDM-purified protein is reconstituted by Sephadex G-50 detergent removal, one freeze/thaw and 0.8-um extrusion. Dilute 10 ul vesicles into 190 ul EDTA-free buffer at 25 C. Following a 1-min baseline, add 5 mM MgCl2 for the WT/empty and protein-loading comparisons. The separate MgCl2 series uses 0.75, 1.5, 3 and 5 mM. Monitor 330/369-nm excitation and 509-nm emission for 10 min; Triton/EDTA calibration yields intravesicular magnesium. Captions report three independent measurements, mean +/- SEM.

evidence.explanation: Figure 6a, its empty-liposome control and reconstitution Methods were inspected; the graph retains the measured compartment and intact construct.
Accession, taxon, full-length sequence equality and current domain interval identify the tested protein, not an isolated-domain experiment.

edges.mechanism: Protein-containing liposomes accumulate magnesium above the empty-vesicle response after MgCl2 addition. The purified reconstitution supports a direct transport-associated effect without proving a specific counterion, native direction or isolated-domain sufficiency.
edges.subject: ttcorb-reconstituted

evidence.explanation: Visually inspected Supplementary Figure 8a and its caption show the protein-loading series with an empty-vesicle baseline.

edges.mechanism: At fixed external magnesium, vesicles prepared with higher TtCorB loading have greater magnesium accumulation across the 1:810, 1:270, 1:90 and 1:30 wt/wt series. This is a loading-dependent ensemble response, not turnover normalized to active oriented protein.
edges.subject: higher-protein-loading

evidence.explanation: Visually inspected Supplementary Figure 8b and transport Methods support the concentration-dependent response without a kinetic-fit claim.

edges.mechanism: Higher external MgCl2 produces greater intravesicular accumulation across the separate 0.75-to-5-mM series. The intervention changes the available substrate and gradient together; it does not isolate binding affinity or establish transport saturation.
edges.subject: higher-external-magnesium

causal_graphs.family_mapping: A0A0K6IWT9 sequence version 1 is 445 aa and maps to PF01595 at 19-189. UniProt and InterPro sequences exactly match. The paper identifies this accession and intact pET29a construct. CBS/CorC regions are also present; the isolated Pfam domain was not tested.
causal_graphs.limitations: Directness concerns magnesium accumulation in purified-protein vesicles, not an observed atomic transport cycle. Orientation and active fraction are not measured, so influx into these vesicles is not native cellular import/export direction. Independent measurements are not stated to be independent purifications. Empty controls receive matched 0.05% UDM buffer. The concentration/loading series are separate interventions, not a serial causal chain or a fitted Michaelis constant. Ion counter-substrates and exchange stoichiometry remain unresolved.

causal_graphs.context: POPE/POPG 3:1, protein/lipid 1:30 wt/wt, encapsulated 50 uM mag-fura-2, pH 7.5 with 100 mM KCl and 50 mM NaCl. After a 1-min baseline at 25 C, add 5 mM MgCl2 and follow calibrated intravesicular magnesium for 10 min. Empty liposomes receive matched 0.05% UDM buffer. Three independent measurements, mean +/- SEM; reconstitution Methods call MtCorB UDM-purified, whereas purification Methods specify DDM.

evidence.explanation: Figure 6a, full-length cloning labels and transport Methods support the positive MtCorB response while preserving the unresolved detergent notation.
The paper accession and matching database sequence identify the archaeal intact construct separately from TtCorB and domain-only constructs.

edges.mechanism: MtCorB-containing vesicles give a modest positive magnesium-accumulation response above empty vesicles after external MgCl2 addition. This is an intact-protein reconstitution result, not an isolated-domain or physiological-direction demonstration.
edges.subject: mtcorb-reconstituted

causal_graphs.family_mapping: A0A1G8XA46 sequence version 1, 426 aa, NCBITaxon 2200; current PF01595 13-187, verified by exact UniProt/InterPro sequence equality. The Pfam interval is not identical to structural TM residues 1-154. Neither isolated CBS 199-322 nor the delta-C structure inherits this full-length transport assay.
causal_graphs.limitations: The smaller MtCorB signal relative to TtCorB is not zero function or evidence of an intrinsically slower transporter; lipid compatibility may differ. The purification/reconstitution detergent discrepancy remains unresolved. Protein orientation, counterion and stoichiometry are not established. No archaeal cellular direction or human CNNM transport claim is inferred.

edges.mechanism: P121G lowers magnesium accumulation in the intact protein. Residual transport and the absence of a direct conformational-motion measurement prevent describing the phenotype as proof of a specific helix-kink mechanism.

evidence.explanation: Figure 6e and Supplementary 8c/d support the scoped decrease and the retained limitations.

edges.mechanism: K122A lowers accumulation relative to WT, with a nonzero signal above empty vesicles. The net response does not identify a unique ion path or distinguish catalytic effects from changes in active fraction.
edges.subject: k122a

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Reference A0A0K6IWT9 S26, S30, N76, S117, E118, P121 and K122 were sequence-verified and all lie inside PF01595 19-189. Each mutation is in the full 445-aa protein, not an isolated-domain construct; domain position does not isolate its causal microstep.
causal_graphs.limitations: All plotted loss-of-response mutants retain accumulation above empty controls. E33A and N80A are described as near WT, not zero-effect proof. Several variants, especially S26A/S30A/N76A, have earlier or broadened SEC peaks. Strong incorporation bands do not establish equal folding, oligomerization, orientation or active fraction. Directness means the net purified-vesicle effect; an elementary metal-coordination or pi-helix-motion mechanism remains unresolved.
